content.text: Understanding core data structures is the foundation of computer science and software engineering. Each data structure offers different trade-offs in terms of time complexity, space usage, and operational characteristics. Mastering these fundamentals enables you to choose the right tool for any problem and reason about algorithmic performance in interviews and production systems.

items: Big O Notation — Asymptotic analysis, time and space complexity, and amortized analysis
Hash Tables — Hash functions, collision resolution, load factors, and real-world implementations
Linked Lists — Singly/doubly linked lists, operations, and classic interview problems
Heap — Binary heaps, priority queues, heap sort, and top-K problems
Queue — FIFO queues, deques, circular buffers, and BFS applications
Ring Buffer — Circular buffer implementation, producer-consumer patterns
Sets — Set operations, implementations, and algorithmic applications
Trie — Prefix trees, autocomplete, and string-based search structures
